summary.oneLiner: Indian renewable energy company that develops, owns and operates wind and solar power generation assets, selling power to industrial & commercial consumers and state-owned DISCOMs.
summary.business: Orient Green Power Company Limited generates and sells power from renewable energy sources — wind and solar — through a network of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries. As of March 31, 2026 the company's aggregate installed capacity was 396 MW, comprising 389 MW of wind power and a 7 MW solar plant commissioned in December 2025, its first entry into solar. Customers are Industrial & Commercial consumers and state-owned DISCOMs.

endMarkets: Industrial & Commercial (C&I) consumers|State-owned DISCOMs|National — 4 Indian states|International — 1 country

currentContext.strengths: Operates in the rapidly growing renewable energy sector, benefiting from increasing electricity demand and regulatory support.|Flexible business model that is scalable and sustainable, enabling predictable growth from a diversified and balanced portfolio of wind and solar projects.|Experienced management and operating team with relevant industry knowledge and expertise, including ability to improve operational performance.|Long association and established track record of good service with customers, positioning the company as a preferred supplier.|Improving financial health, with operating SPVs receiving investment-grade (BBB-) rating from Credit Rating Agencies.
currentContext.strategies: Focused on developing, owning and operating renewable energy (wind and solar) generation assets in India.|Diversifying into solar power alongside the existing wind portfolio, having commissioned its first solar plant in FY26.|Improving operating efficiencies through repowering of old wind turbines with higher-capacity rated machines.|Progressive repayment of term debt to reduce interest expense, improve credit ratings and access lower-cost borrowings to fund expansion plans.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26, the company diversified into solar power, commissioning its first solar plant (7 MW) in December 2025 as part of a planned 25 MW AC solar capacity being developed through subsidiary Delta Renewable Energy Private Limited; the balance 18 MW is underway and expected to be completed before September 2026. On the wind side, the company completed a wind portfolio expansion of 9.9 MW using larger-capacity wind turbines, and initiated repowering of old windmills at the Devarkulam Site, Tamil Nadu through step-down subsidiary Clarion Wind Farm Private Limited — an initial 6.3 MW contract followed by a further 1.5 MW executed in April 2026, taking total repowering capacity to 7.8 MW — the first repowering project under the Government of Tamil Nadu's new repowering policy; this repowered capacity is expected to be commissioned in FY27. The BRSR disclosure notes that component upgradation of certain identified windmills and capacity-enhancement initiatives are expected to improve green energy generation, with the majority of the company's R&D and capex investment directed toward technologies that improve environmental and social impact.
currentContext.mdna: Government of India's target of 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030, with National Generation Adequacy Plan projecting renewable capacity of about 764 GW required by 2035-36, seen as providing ample opportunity for business growth.|Increasing demand from Industrial & Commercial (C&I) customers for renewable power to reduce their carbon footprint, expected to support business expansion.|India's power demand projected to grow above 6% per the National Generation Adequacy Plan (2026-27 to 2035-36), with capacity requirement projected at 1,121 GW.|Strong wind availability during the FY26 wind season, combined with resumption of windmills that had undergone component upgradation, drove improved operational performance during the year.|Improved credit ratings (BBB-) and liquidity position the company to raise new borrowings at lower interest rates to fund expansion.|Business remains exposed to weaknesses such as market-based electricity pricing, seasonality/weather dependence, reliance on OEMs for windmill maintenance, and continued high upfront capital requirements for renewable technology.|18 MW solar capacity project underway (balance of the 25 MW AC project via subsidiary Delta Renewable Energy Private Limited), expected to be completed before September 2026.|7.8 MW of wind repowering underway at the Devarkulam Site, Tamil Nadu via step-down subsidiary Clarion Wind Farm Private Limited, expected to be completed in fiscal 2026-27.

risks.note: Transmission, evacuation constraints and grid back-down issues can curtail the power the company is able to dispatch, directly affecting generation and revenue.

Changing government policies on power pricing and Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs), and an uncertain regulatory regime, can impact tariffs and demand for the company's power; evolving policy changes and ongoing disputes with Discoms continue to pose challenges, though many have been addressed through formal representations.
Delays in recovery of dues from state-owned distribution companies (Discoms) may result in acute working capital shortages.
Continuing technological advancements and cost reductions in solar and newer wind power could make the company's existing plants comparatively obsolete or unviable.
The company's capital structure includes significant amounts borrowed from banks and financial institutions; an increase in interest rates would affect profitability.

Reliance on OEMs and other service providers for maintaining windmills and supplying critical spares/components is a significant challenge that may lead to increased maintenance costs and higher downtime; the company is progressively developing alternative sources to reduce this dependence.

risks.risk: Capital intensity of repowering old windmills
risks.note: Repowering old windmills with higher-capacity machines to improve efficiency involves significant capital investment.

risks.risk: Asset ageing and business continuity risk
risks.note: Assets installed several years ago must compete with newer machines equipped with upgraded technology delivering improved generation and lower maintenance costs; potential threats such as natural disasters, wars or technical failures also exist despite preparedness, mitigated through insurance cover, preventive maintenance and repowering.

one-line thesis: A turned-around, sub-scale wind IPP (399 MW) delivering record FY26 PAT on favorable wind + interest savings, but structurally capped near ~50 MW of organic growth without an external equity raise it has repeatedly failed to close — the 1 GW ambition remains aspirational and offtaker/wind-variability risk persists.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Q4 FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR 316 cr | +13% | INR 46 cr | marginally lower |
| EBITDA | INR 206 cr | +10% | INR 18 cr | marginally lower |
| PAT | INR 72 cr (record high) | +70% | Loss before exceptional & tax INR (16.4) cr | vs INR (14.7) cr LY |
| Interest cost | down ~21% (debt decline + 45 bps rate cut on main loan) | — | — | — |
| Operating capacity | 399 MW (392 MW wind + 7 MW solar) | — | — | — |

One-offs / drivers: (a) refund of excess interest charged in earlier periods boosted FY26; (b) Q4 hit by below-normal wind (seasonally weakest quarter); (c) ~INR 1 cr higher depreciation on new capitalization in Q4; (d) ~INR 1.67 cr one-time write-off of long-overdue item + higher legal/consultancy in Q4 other expenses; (e) new wind assets carry free O&M in year one.
guidance (next quarter / fy27):
- Management explicitly refuses sequential QoQ guidance — says renewables must be compared YoY (same quarter prior year), not QoQ, due to wind seasonality. Use Q1 FY26 as the reference for Q1 FY27.
- 9.9 MW wind (6.6 MW commissioned Mar'26, 3.3 MW Apr'26) fully available for the wind season starting end-May; 7 MW solar available all year.
- 17.6 MW solar under construction: commissioned Q1 FY27, full production Q2 FY27.
- Revenue/EBITDA on a full-year basis: 17.6 MW solar ≈ INR 14.5 cr rev / INR 12.8 cr EBITDA; 9.9 MW wind ≈ INR 14 cr rev / INR 10 cr EBITDA (both at normal weather; FY27 partial-year for solar).
- No 1 GW timeline given — "market too volatile," may update "next quarter or so."
order book & pipeline:
- No conventional order book (IPP). Pipeline = capacity additions: 9.9 MW wind (done), 17.6 MW solar (under construction, FY27), 7.8 MW repowering of older Tamil Nadu turbines under new TN repowering policy (in process).
- Likely to add more repowering capacity during FY27; FY28 additions still work-in-progress.
- 1 GW target: prefers acquiring operating assets (fastest route) but strategic M&A "slowed" amid weak market; focus shifted to internal projects meanwhile.
segment / subsidiary:
- Main operating subsidiary "Beta" carries the largest loan; loan terms sweep most surplus cash flow into accelerated debt prepayment (limits cash available for expansion equity).
- Croatia 10.5 MW wind asset (international diversification).
- Offtake: significant % is C&I (fixed tariff), remainder long-term PPAs; direct SEB exposure only to AP and Gujarat boards.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Repowering older vintage turbines (higher-capacity machines, wind-only or wind+solar hybrid) — newly viable under TN policy; key efficiency lever.
- Battery storage added to solar to convert daytime-only output into 24x7 C&I-friendly supply — under evaluation.
- Solar diversification to balance wind variability — but management deliberately cautious given midday solar grid glut / depressed afternoon prices.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 EBITDA margin ~65% (206/316); structurally high as expected for an asset-heavy IPP.
- Interest cost down ~21% is the standout earnings driver (deleveraging + 45 bps rate cut).
- Year-one free O&M on new assets supports near-term margins; interest on new wind loans will start dragging.
- Tariffs fixed through the year (C&I + long-term PPA), so revenue swings are volume (wind)-driven, not price-driven.
capex / expansion:
- Funded organically: 9.9 MW wind + 17.6 MW solar + 7.8 MW repowering all from internal resources.
- Hard ceiling: only ~50 MW of further additions feasible without raising external equity. New capacity takes 6–8 months to build; FY27 plan already locked.
capital allocation:
- Loan covenants force surplus cash into early debt repayment (esp. subsidiary Beta) — this is automatic, not discretionary.
- No dividend; investor pressed on debt-free/dividend path — management says deleveraging happens anyway but won't fund large expansion.
- Equity options for 1 GW (preferential / rights / strategic / possible foreign investor while retaining control) all "on the table" but nothing announceable; two prior rights issues have not delivered shareholder returns.
- Management concedes the stock is undervalued vs listed renewable peers on PE/EV-EBITDA.
risks & watch-items:
- **Wind variability** — single biggest earnings swing factor; Q4 FY26 shows downside; sector-wide, not OGPL-specific.
- **Equity-raise execution risk** — repeatedly deferred; without it, growth and re-rating stall; promoter-stake constraints limit options.
- **SEB receivables** — AP (prior issues, now smoother) and Gujarat (clean); centre pressuring SEBs to pay on time; flagged but currently low.
- **Solar oversupply / midday price glut** — caps solar expansion economics.
- **Curtailment** — only minor technical curtailment so far; monitor during peak wind season.
- **Capital starvation by design** — cash sweep to debt leaves little for growth equity.
management quality / tone:
- Candid and measured; CEO openly acknowledges undervaluation, equity-raise setbacks, and the structural growth ceiling rather than over-promising.
- Repeatedly deflects price/valuation and timeline questions citing listed-company disclosure norms — disciplined, not evasive.
- Investor frustration evident (Faisal Hawa) over stalled 1 GW target and lack of returns after two rights issues; management empathetic but non-committal.
non-obvious takeaways:
- FY26's record PAT is partly non-recurring: the excess-interest refund and an unusually strong H1 wind season flatter the year — quality of the +70% PAT is lower than headline.
- The cash-sweep loan structure means equity holders cannot expect dividends or rapid deleveraging-to-FCF; value accrues to lenders first.
- Management is effectively signaling the asset may be monetized/partnered (PE fund, foreign investor) rather than grown organically — a potential strategic-event optionality more than an organic-growth story.
- "Compare YoY not QoQ" framing is a genuine analytical guardrail for modeling this stock.

| SEB receivable risk (AP, Gujarat) | GREENPOWER · 533263 (improving) | — | Self: centre-driven SEB payment discipline easing a historic overhang. Low |
qoq change log:
- New since prior calls: first solar plant (7 MW, Dec'25) commissioned; 9.9 MW wind added (6.6 MW Mar'26 + 3.3 MW Apr'26); 17.6 MW solar under construction (FY27); 7.8 MW TN repowering initiated under new policy.
- FY26 PAT INR 72 cr = record high (+70% YoY), aided by interest refund + 21% lower interest cost (45 bps rate cut on main loan + lower debt).
- Q4 FY26 weaker YoY (income INR 46 cr, EBITDA INR 18 cr; pre-exceptional loss widened to INR 16.4 cr from 14.7 cr) on below-normal wind + INR 1.67 cr one-off write-off + higher legal/consultancy.
- Credit rating/outlook upgraded for key subsidiaries during FY26.
- 1 GW target reiterated but timeline withdrawn ("market too volatile"); strategic M&A explicitly "slowed."
- New strategic tone: explicit openness to PE/foreign-investor structures while retaining control; battery storage under evaluation.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
